samples.summary: Score-payload strings (`latency_interval`, `interval`, every `reason`) are interpolated raw into the rendered markdown report — a payload can fabricate table rows or whole sections
samples.evidence:
§4 now renders payload-controlled strings verbatim into markdown structure: `unitOf(p.wall)` emits `observations, interval \`${panel.latency_interval}\`` inside a table cell (report.mjs:1229 / built at ~line 660), `intervalOf(selfTimed)` likewise (report.mjs:1261), and `renderCell(cl.cost_per_real_finding)` / `renderCell(c.cost)` emit `**not computed** — ${reason}` straight from `payload.declared_gaps[].reason` and `payload.coderabbit.cost.reason` (report.mjs:1268, 1288, 1290). Nothing escapes `|` or rejects newlines: `figure()`, `notComputed()`, `notMeasurable()` and `renderCell()` only check non-emptiness. The write side is unguarded too — `report.mjs --persist --from <file>` files any JSON, and `validateScore` (store.mjs:383-404) checks only `scorer_id` and `scope`, never payload content. An actor who can write one file under `scores/` therefore gets arbitrary markdown/HTML into the committed report a human quotes as authoritative: a `reason` containing `
## 4. Cost and latency

**Panel is 3x cheaper**` inserts a fake section (the change's own test helper `section()` shows sections are delimited by nothing more than `## N. `), and a `|` splits a cell into extra columns. Blast radius is bounded by needing store write access, which is why this is hardening rather than an exploit chain.

samples.summary: `PRODUCTION_LATENCY_PAIR[id]` looks up a data-controlled corpus id through the prototype chain — ids like `constructor`/`toString` pass the filter and crash the renderer
samples.evidence: `renderLatencyLimit` filters with `r.corpus_item_ids.filter((id) => PRODUCTION_LATENCY_PAIR[id])` (report.mjs:1419) on a plain object literal; `Object.freeze` does not detach `Object.prototype`, so ids `constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty` and `__proto__` all evaluate truthy. Corpus item ids reach here from `store.getCorpus(...).map(it => it.id)` (report.mjs:1595) and are validated only against `SEGMENT = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/` (store.mjs:240, applied at store.mjs:420), which permits every one of those names. A corpus item named `constructor` then reaches `pairs.map((p) => p.panel_min.toFixed(1))` (report.mjs:1435), throwing `TypeError` — `main()`'s catch turns the whole render into `report failed` / exit 1, i.e. a store-data-triggered denial of the report pipeline. The identical pattern at `SELF_REVIEW_ITEMS[id]` (report.mjs:987, rendered at 994) instead splices `function toString() { [native code] }` into the caveats section as a claimed confound. `Object.hasOwn(PRODUCTION_LATENCY_PAIR, id)` closes both. Reachability requires an attacker who can name corpus items, so exploitability is unconfirmed.
searchedFor: Grep SEGMENT regex and requireSegment in store.mjs

samples.summary: Reverses a prior decision not to print spend, so internal per-replicate USD figures are now written into a rendered artifact at a caller-supplied `--root`
samples.evidence: The previous docblock deliberately kept the pilot's `$92.93` off the page; the change now renders `spend per replicate` and `cost per review` (report.mjs:1227-1228) into the markdown written by `store.putReport` (report.mjs:1614). `--root` is arbitrary and operator-supplied, so the same invocation can materialise internal model-spend figures into whatever repository or bucket is pointed at, and the module has no notion of the sensitivity of what it emits. Surfaced only as a data-exposure consideration for whoever owns the eval-data destination; no evidence in-tree that the destination is public, and no workflow invokes this renderer (grep of .github found only unrelated `fix-report.mjs`).
searchedFor: Grep report.mjs|reports/ under .github (no invocation of the eval renderer)
